cls: Endogenous methyl donor / hepatoprotective; stable salt form of S-adenosylmethionine
pharm: Used for intrahepatic cholestasis and as adjunctive treatment in depression and osteoarthritis
tags: not FDA-approved as drug (EU/India Rx; US supplement)
quick: Oral 800-1600 mg/day; IV/IM 200-800 mg/day (as ademetionine ion)
Enteric-coated tablets between meals, in the morning
Used for cholestasis of pregnancy under supervision
Used in cholestasis; monitor liver function
summary: S-adenosyl-L-methionine disulfate tosylate is a stabilised salt form of ademetionine (SAMe), the principal biological methyl donor and a glutathione precursor. It is used in the EU and several countries (and as a supplement in the US) for intrahepatic cholestasis (including cholestasis of pregnancy) and as adjunctive therapy in depression and osteoarthritis. Doses are expressed as the ademetionine ion: oral 800-1600 mg/day or parenteral 200-800 mg/day. It is generally well tolerated; caution is needed in bipolar disorder (mania switch) and methionine-cycle defects. It is not FDA-approved as a drug.
indications: Intrahepatic cholestasis (including intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy)
Symptomatic treatment of osteoarthritis (joint pain) where licensed/used

dosage.d: 800-1600 mg/day orally (parenteral 200-400 mg/day initially in some protocols)

admin: Swallow enteric-coated tablets whole; take between meals, preferably in the morning
Do not crush or chew enteric-coated tablets
Reconstitute parenteral form immediately before use per product instructions
Avoid taking late in the day (may be activating and disturb sleep)
Use under medical supervision, particularly in pregnancy and mood disorders
moa: Ademetionine (SAMe) is the principal physiological methyl-group donor in transmethylation reactions and a precursor in transsulphuration (to glutathione, a major antioxidant) and aminopropylation (polyamine synthesis). In cholestasis it restores hepatocyte membrane fluidity and bile salt transport; its CNS effects in depression are attributed to enhanced methylation and monoamine synthesis.

absolute: Genetic defects of the methionine cycle causing homocystinuria/hyperhomocysteinaemia (e.g. cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency)
relative: Bipolar disorder (risk of switch to mania/hypomania)
Concomitant serotonergic drugs (theoretical serotonin syndrome risk)
monitor: Mood for manic switch or agitation
Vitamin B12/folate status with long-term use (homocysteine handling)

preg: Ademetionine has been used to treat intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy under specialist supervision and is generally considered acceptable when clearly needed; use only on medical advice.
lact: Data during breastfeeding are limited; use with caution and only if the benefit justifies potential risk.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is well established; use with general caution in significant renal impairment.
hepatic: Used therapeutically in intrahepatic cholestasis; monitor liver function. No reduction is generally required, but supervise hepatic response.

moderate: Serotonergic agents (SSRIs, SNRIs, MAOIs, tramadol, triptans) - theoretical additive serotonergic effect / serotonin syndrome
minor: May affect homocysteine handling - consider adequate B12/folate
interactions.food: Take enteric-coated tablets between meals for better absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol to reduce hepatic stress.
interactions.diagnostics: May influence plasma homocysteine; generally minimal effect on routine tests.

emergency: Manic or psychotic episode in bipolar disorder
Possible serotonin syndrome with serotonergic combinations

monitoring: Mood and behaviour, especially for manic switch
Sleep and agitation early in treatment
counsel: Take the enteric-coated tablets whole, between meals, preferably in the morning
Tell your doctor if you have bipolar disorder - this medicine can trigger mania
Avoid taking it late in the day if it disturbs your sleep
Report severe agitation, palpitations or a rash
This is not an FDA-approved drug in the US, where it is sold as a supplement
pk: Cholestatic and mood effects develop over days to weeks
Store below 25 C, protected from moisture; reconstitute parenteral just before use
pearls: Disulfate tosylate is a stable salt of SAMe used to ensure adequate shelf-life and oral bioavailability
Not FDA-approved as a drug; Rx in the EU/India for cholestasis, OTC supplement in the US
Doses are conventionally expressed as the ademetionine (SAMe) ion
Use cautiously in bipolar disorder - can precipitate mania
Theoretical serotonin syndrome risk with serotonergic antidepressants
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless it is close to the next dose; then skip it and resume. Do not double up. Avoid taking a delayed dose late in the evening because it may disturb sleep.
overdose: Overdose data are limited; SAMe is an endogenous compound with a wide margin of safety. Excess may cause GI upset, anxiety or agitation. Manage with supportive care.
